newsitem.title: USA: Mexico scoffs at money-laundering guesstimate.
newsitem.headline: Mexico scoffs at money-laundering guesstimate.

text.p: Mexican Finance Secretarty Guillermo Ortiz on Wednesday scoffed on Wednesday at an often -repeated estimate that Mexico's financial system launders $30 billion of drug money every year.
Asked at a news conference whether he thought that such a calculation was correct, Ortiz replied: "Frankly, I don't have the slightest idea. But the number seems a tad exaggerated".
"If such amounts (were flowing into Mexico), our balance of payments figures would be very different," he added.

U.S. diplomats and law enforcement officials have quoted the $30 billion figure in testimony before Congress, prompting lawmakers to demand more cooperation from Mexico to fight drug trafficking and stamp out corruption.

One State Department official last month told a congressional panel that "roughly $30 billion in drug cash was repatriated to Mexican drug cartels during 1994". However, he cited "Mexican officials" as the source for that figure.
The United States and Mexico have squabbled in the past over drug data, such as the U.S. estimate that some 70 percent of all cocaine is smuggled from Mexican territory.
Despite their ocassional spats, the two governments recognize that they must cooperate.

Ortiz acknowledged that Mexico would accept $250,000 in computer equipment and training from the United States, which will provide the Mexican government with seed money to set up a financial analysis unit to investigate money laundering.
Mexico is currently passing legislation to criminalize money laundering, which entails disguising illegal earnings through financial transactions.
